Cave of Machpelah
mak-PEE-luh
proper noun (Old Testament place)
Machpelah (Hebrew Makhpelah) means "double" or "doubled," perhaps from the cave's twofold chamber; the field and cave near Mamre at Hebron.

📖 Biblical Definition

The cave of Machpelah was the burying place of the patriarchs, the field and cave that Abraham bought of Ephron the Hittite for a possession of a buryingplace, when Sarah died at Kirjath-arba, which is Hebron, in the land of Canaan. Though God had promised Abraham the whole land, in his lifetime he possessed not so much as to set his foot on, save this one field, which he purchased openly before the sons of Heth for four hundred shekels of silver, current money with the merchant. He would not take it as a gift but bought it outright, that he might have a sure title in the land of promise. There Abraham buried Sarah; there afterward Abraham himself was buried, and Isaac and Rebekah, and Leah, and Jacob, whose body Joseph and his brethren carried up out of Egypt to lay in the cave with his fathers. The purchase of Machpelah is a true history and a great act of faith: by securing a grave in Canaan, the patriarchs confessed that they believed the promise of the land, and that they looked beyond their own deaths to the resurrection and the inheritance God had sworn. They died in faith, not having received the promises, but having seen them afar off and embraced them, confessing they were strangers and pilgrims, and so the cave became a standing pledge of the covenant and a witness to the hope of resurrection.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The field and cave at Hebron that Abraham bought for a burying place, where the patriarchs and their wives were laid in hope of the promise.

CAVE OF MACHPELAH, proper noun. From the Hebrew Makhpelah, "double"; the field and cave near Mamre at Hebron.

Purchased by Abraham of Ephron the Hittite as a possession of a buryingplace.

The resting place of Abraham, Sarah, Isaac, Rebekah, Leah, and Jacob.

As it is written, "the field, and the cave that is therein, were made sure unto Abraham for a possession of a buryingplace by the sons of Heth" (Gen 23:20).

A pledge of faith in the promise of the land and the hope of resurrection.

📖 Key Scripture

Gen 23:9 — "That he may give me the cave of Machpelah, which he hath, which is in the end of his field; for as much money as it is worth he shall give it me for a possession of a buryingplace amongst you."

Gen 23:19 — "And after this, Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the cave of the field of Machpelah before Mamre: the same is Hebron in the land of Canaan."

Gen 23:20 — "And the field, and the cave that is therein, were made sure unto Abraham for a possession of a buryingplace by the sons of Heth."

Gen 49:31 — "There they buried Abraham and Sarah his wife; there they buried Isaac and Rebekah his wife; and there I buried Leah."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Machpelah faces no postmodern redefinition, but the patriarchs' faith in the promise and the resurrection is too little pondered.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The biblical principle to recover is the patriarchal faith that bought a grave in Canaan as a pledge of God's promise. Abraham, owning no more of the promised land than this one field, paid full price for it rather than receive it as a gift, that he might hold a sure title and so confess his faith that his seed would inherit the whole. He died in faith, not having received the promise, but having seen it afar off.

The deeper lesson is the hope of resurrection. The patriarchs were laid in Machpelah not as men without hope but as those who believed God would keep covenant with them and their seed and raise them up at the last. To purchase a burying place in the land of promise was to plant a stake of faith in the soil of God's word. So the cave teaches the believer to face death as a sojourner who waits, sure of the inheritance reserved in heaven and of the resurrection of the body.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

The purchase is rooted in the Abrahamic covenant of the land and in the patriarchs' faith in the resurrection.

expand to see more

God had promised the land of Canaan to Abraham and his seed (Gen 13:15).

Sarah's death at Hebron occasioned the purchase of the burying place (Gen 23:2).

Abraham bought field and cave of Ephron for four hundred shekels (Gen 23:16).

Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and their wives were buried there (Gen 49:31).

Jacob's body was carried from Egypt to rest with his fathers (Gen 50:13).

Usage

"Machpelah is cited as the one foothold Abraham held in the promised land."

"The purchase is read as an act of faith in the covenant of the land."

"The patriarchs' graves are invoked as witnesses to the hope of resurrection."
